A. The payee's leverage is the product: INSIGHT: Payees do not want a payment rail; they want a threat they can hold. A digital cheque that weakens the s.138 threat without giving equal assurance loses the payee, and the payee decides whether a cheque is used.
B. Fights are about why the money was ow: INSIGHT: Most disputes are about the story behind the cheque, and the cheque never records that story. The instrument carries an amount and a signature but not the debt it is meant to prove.
C. Clocks and delivery decide outcomes: INSIGHT: Cases are won and lost on dates and proof of delivery that nobody tracks for the payee. The return memo starts a legal clock without saying so.
D. Trust is checked too late, by the wro: INSIGHT: Every Indian check on a cheque serves the bank at presentation, never the payee at acceptance. The payee takes the cheque blind.
E. Courts are leverage, not a remedy: INSIGHT: In Gujarat, a cheque case averages about ten years, so s.138 works as pressure to settle rather than a way to get paid. The real resolution happens outside the courtroom.
F. Payers lose sight and control once a: INSIGHT: After handing over a cheque, the payer cannot see it, and the only way to stop it still counts as dishonour. Control exists on paper but carries legal risk.
G. The door is open, but nothing is desi: INSIGHT: The regulator has signalled e-cheques but specified nothing, and no Indian model exists. Adoption will depend on both sides joining at once, so it has to start in closed networks.
